title: Mike Hammer
paragraphs: Radio adventures based on Mickey Spillane's hard-boiled detective Mike Hammer, represented largely by the 1953 series That Hammer Guy and its violent, fast-moving criminal cases.

Mutual radio adaptation of Mickey Spillane Mike Hammer. Frozen GRH subset contains eight preservation objects with collector-title/date conflicts, including two distinct Jolie copies and distinct Dead Dame/Hammer Framed recordings.

GRH documents the program through Larry Haines era (1953 to 1953) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] and Ted de Corsia era (1954 to 1954) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Larry Haines (performer on 5 recordings), Ed Ladd (announcer on 2 recordings), Edward Adamson (writer on 2 recordings), Mickey Spillane (creator on 2 recordings), Richard Lewis (director on 2 recordings), Ted de Corsia (performer on 2 recordings), and Jan Miner (performer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include hard-boiled private-eye noir, murder investigation, violent criminal underworld, Mutual network detective radio, and collector title and transfer variants.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including That Hammer Guy on Mutual and Fragmentary Mike Hammer radio survival and collector aliases.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|cloak-and-dagger|Cloak and Dagger]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]] (2 shared credited people), and [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (2 shared credited people).
